```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dunn.test)
library(readxl)
```

```{r}
df <- read_xlsx("Oospore_data.xlsx", na = "NA")
```

# 1. Morphology --\> size

## 1.1 Mean
```{r}
morph <- df %>% filter(assay == "morphology")

#Overall mean
morph %>%
  summarize(mean_diam = mean(mean_diam_um, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_diam = sd(mean_diam_um, na.rm = TRUE))
```

**Mean Diam:** 38.46 Standard dev diam: 7.62

```{r}
#Per isolate
morph %>%
  group_by(isolate) %>%
  summarize(mean_diam = mean(mean_diam_um, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_diam = sd(mean_diam_um, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n())
```

| Isolate | Mean diam | Sd diam |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| 21007   | 35.65     | 4.84    |
| 22031   | 34.06     | 5.12    |
| 25248   | 45.67     | 6.75    |

## 1.2 Range
```{r}
morph %>%
  summarize(min_diam = min(mean_diam_um, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_diam = max(mean_diam_um, na.rm = TRUE))
```
Range: 25.446 um to 61.8545um

```{r}
morph %>%
  group_by(isolate) %>%
  summarize(min_diam = min(mean_diam_um, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_diam = max(mean_diam_um, na.rm = TRUE))

```
 Isolate | min diam | max diam |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| 21007   | 25.46    | 52.51    |
| 22031   | 25.45     | 49.00    |
| 25248   | 28.50     | 61.86    |

## 1.3 Are any isolates significantly differently sized than the others?

```{r}
# Check normality per isolate
morph %>%
  group_by(isolate) %>%
  summarize(p_shapiro = shapiro.test(mean_diam_um)$p.value)

# if p>0.05 for all isolates use ANOVA
# if p<0.05 for any, use Kruskal-Wallis 
```

Two isolates (21007 and 22031) failed the normality test (p\<0.05) so we should use Kruskal-Wallis

```{r}
kruskal.test(mean_diam_um ~ factor(isolate), data = morph)
```

Note:

- ANOVA assumes your data is normally distributed.

- Kruskal-Wallils is the non parametric equivalent, so it doesn't assume normality. Instead of comparing means, it ranks all the values and compares those ranks across groups.

```{r}
# post hoc test 
dunn.test(morph$mean_diam_um, morph$isolate, method = "bonferroni")
```

Note:

- For ANOVA the post hoc test is Tukey HSD

- For Kruskal its dunns test Both compare every possible pair of gropus to find which pairs are different

| Comparison     | P value    | Take away                                   |
|----------------|------------|---------------------------------------------|
| 21007 vs 22031 | p = 0.1052 | not significantly different in oospore size |
| 21007 vs 25248 | p \~ 0     | 25248 is sig larger then 21007              |
| 22031 vs 25248 | p \~ 0     | 25248 is sig larger then 22031              |

**Take away**: 21007 and 22031 produced similarly size oospores, and 25248 produces significantly larger oospores than the other two isolates

## 1.2 Box plot

```{r}
# y position of significance letters
letters_df <- data.frame(
  isolate = factor(c("21007", "22031", "25248")),
  label = c("a", "a", "b"),
  y = c(56, 53, 65)  # adjust these values as needed
)

box <- ggplot(morph, aes(x = factor(isolate), y = mean_diam_um)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = letters_df, aes(x = isolate, y = y, label = label),
            size = 4) +
  labs(x = "Isolate", y = "Mean oospore diameter (µm)") +
  theme_classic()

print(box)
ggsave("Plot_oospore.png", box, dpi = 600, width = 6.5, height = 4.5, units = "in")
```

```{r}
# check outliers
morph %>%
  group_by(isolate) %>%
  summarize(
    Q1 = quantile(mean_diam_um, 0.25),
    Q3 = quantile(mean_diam_um, 0.75),
    IQR = IQR(mean_diam_um),
    lower_fence = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR,
    upper_fence = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
  )
```

```{r}
# identify specific outliers
morph %>%
  group_by(isolate) %>%
  filter(mean_diam_um > quantile(mean_diam_um, 0.75) + 1.5 * IQR(mean_diam_um) |
         mean_diam_um < quantile(mean_diam_um, 0.25) - 1.5 * IQR(mean_diam_um)) %>%
  select(isolate, oospore_num, mean_diam_um)
```

#2. Plasmolysis --\> viability

```{r}
plasm <- df %>% filter(assay == "plasmolysis")

# Overall 
plasm %>%
  summarize(viable = sum(viable, na.rm = TRUE),
            total = n(),
            pct_viable = viable / total * 100)
```

```{r}
# Per isolate
plasm %>%
  group_by(isolate) %>%
  summarize(viable = sum(viable, na.rm = TRUE),
            total = n(),
            pct_viable = viable / total * 100)
```

## 2.1 Does viability differ across isolates?

```{r}
# Build contingency table
plasm_table <- plasm %>%
  group_by(isolate) %>%
  summarize(viable = sum(viable),
            not_viable = n() - sum(viable)) %>%
  column_to_rownames("isolate") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Chi-square test
chisq.test(plasm_table)
```

Note:

- chi square test asks whether the distribution of counts across categories differs from what you would expect by chance.

- Does viability depend on which isolate we're looking at

**Takeaway**: - p=0.867 - viability is not sig. different across isolates. - All three isolates have statistically similar vaibility rates
